items.question: What supreme attainment makes one dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are valued attainments
Great accomplishment is a supreme attainment
Such accomplishment can make one dear to yoginis
items.inference: One who attains great accomplishment in enjoyment and liberation may become dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginis through the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes after the teaching on the moon island?
premises: The teaching has emerged in the context of Candra-dvipa
Chapters are numbered sequentially
This section is identified as the ninth
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes after the teaching that emerged in Candra-dvipa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvipa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is to be contemplated in a specific posture
Fire surrounds the self in this visualization
The posture involves standing on one foot
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the deity regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly
The determination of knowledge is sought
The request is for it to be made manifest now
items.inference: The speaker asks the deity to make the determination of knowledge manifest now.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me now.

items.question: What detailed division of eightfold groups is sought to be fully known?
premises: A division into eight groups of eight is referenced
Complete knowledge of this division is desired
The knowledge is sought in full detail
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and in detail the division of the eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā interpreted as in full detail based on context
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and in detail the division of the eight groups of eight.

items.question: How is the wheel quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: A secret place is the locus of practice
The wheel is the object of accomplishment
Quick accomplishment is possible there
items.inference: In the secret place, O Bhairava, the wheel is quickly accomplished.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the goddess for asking a question rare even for gods?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
He has been asked a question
The question concerns something hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because she has asked about something difficult even for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! You have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with a specific locus
The syllable laṃ is associated with another locus
These loci are the brahmarandhra and the forehead
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ corresponds to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in a specific region
The syllable śa is placed in another region
These regions are the throat and the heart
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region and the syllable śa is in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation remains to be taught
The listener is urged to hear it
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described?
premises: A divine lotus is the object of meditation
It has eight spokes or petals
It is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Meditate on the divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with equanimous mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equanimous mind
Certain conventional conduct is incompatible
Village dharma is to be abandoned
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equanimous mind should abandon village dharma.
uncertainties: grāma-dharma interpreted as conventional village conduct
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equanimous mind, one should abandon the ways of ordinary village life.

items.question: What siddhis arise from this practice, such as distant hearing and binding?
premises: Specific powers result from the practice
Knowledge of distant hearing is one such power
Paralysis of bonds is another power
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham interpreted as paralysis or arrest of bonds
items.plain_english: One gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments, including immortality and transformation, are briefly stated?
premises: Additional powers are being summarized
Immortality is among these attainments
Transformation is also attained
items.inference: In brief, the practice also yields immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O Goddess, in brief one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized in meditation?
premises: A second wheel is being described
It has eight petals
It is brightly illuminated through fiery meditation
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second wheel has eight petals and is brilliantly illuminated through meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
Such focus enables creative power
Multiple forms can be produced
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power does the practitioner possess when angered?
premises: Anger activates a great power
The power extends to the entire triple world
Both moving and unmoving beings are included
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
It has a specific spiritual function
It liberates from the nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva interpreted as nine principles based on common usage
items.plain_english: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: The practice affects bodily aging
Wrinkles and grey hair are removed
Perception extends to very distant things
items.inference: The practice brings destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and likewise the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should one practice in solitude to manifest multiple forms?
premises: Solitude is the prescribed setting
Meditation must be pursued with intent
Multiple forms are to be created
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create forms in many ways.
uncertainties: sandhi in dhyānañ noted but token kept fused
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What attainment comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: Constant practice is required
The practitioner must be devoted to it
Immortality is the result
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: One who is devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death related to aging?
premises: A regimen involving non-eating by day is prescribed
Aging and death are the conditions addressed
The practitioner will overcome them
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death associated with aging.
uncertainties: gamiṣyate interpreted as going beyond or overcoming in this context
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death due to aging.

items.question: What youthful form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant yogic practice is maintained
A specific duration is implied by two times eight years
The practitioner attains a corresponding youthful form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ interpreted as the form of sixteen years
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from constantly contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is the object of contemplation
The contemplation is performed constantly
This practice grants power over the triple world
items.inference: By constantly contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
